# meltcloud_nest_instance (Resource)

A [Nest Instance](https://docs.meltcloud.io/tasks/nest/create-instance) is one host of the Nest. It installs and joins the Nest once the host boots from a `meltcloud_nest_instance_image`; `status` turns from `installing` to `ready` then.

Needs the API Key of the admin Organization. A Nest has at most seven instances.

~> Only an instance that has not joined the Nest can be destroyed. To take out one that has, [reset](https://docs.meltcloud.io/tasks/nest/reset-instance) it in the admin area first; it is `removed` then.

~> After an instance joins, [enable high availability](https://docs.meltcloud.io/tasks/foundry/enable-high-availability) on a single-instance Foundry once three instances are `ready`, or [rebalance](https://docs.meltcloud.io/tasks/foundry/rebalance) a highly available one, in the admin area.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# add a second and a third nest instance, each in a zone of its own
resource "meltcloud_nest_instance" "nest_1" {
  name               = "nest-1"
  zone_id            = meltcloud_zone.zrh_dc2.id
  network_profile_id = meltcloud_network_profile.nest.id

  ip_addresses = [
    { ip_pool_id = meltcloud_ip_pool.hosts.id, address = "10.0.10.11" },
  ]

  boot_disk = {
    device        = "/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-1"
    mirror        = true
    mirror_device = "/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-2"
  }

  etcd_disk = {
    enabled = true
    device  = "/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-3"
  }
}

# on a nest that uses BGP, each instance peers with its routers
resource "meltcloud_nest_instance" "nest_2" {
  name               = "nest-2"
  zone_id            = meltcloud_zone.zrh_dc3.id
  network_profile_id = meltcloud_network_profile.nest.id

  ip_addresses = [
    { ip_pool_id = meltcloud_ip_pool.hosts.id, address = "10.0.10.12" },
  ]

  boot_disk = {
    device = "/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-1"
  }

  bgp = {
    local_asn = 65012
    peers = [
      { ip = "10.0.10.1", asn = 65000, password_wo = var.bgp_password, password_wo_version = 1, bfd = {} },
    ]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `boot_disk` (Attributes) The boot disk of the instance. Changing it replaces the instance (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--boot_disk))
- `ip_addresses` (Attributes Set) [Static IPs](https://docs.meltcloud.io/concepts/networking/subnet-addressing#static-ip-addresses) in the IP Pools of the Network Profile, one per pool. The instance needs one on the primary host network. In the other pools, it gets an address the pool allocates (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ip_addresses))
- `name` (String) Host name of the Nest Instance, unique within the Nest
- `network_profile_id` (Number) ID of the [Network Profile](https://docs.meltcloud.io/concepts/networking/network-profiles) the instance uses
- `zone_id` (Number) ID of the [Zone](https://docs.meltcloud.io/concepts/regions-and-zones) the instance is in. Sets the Kubernetes labels `topology.kubernetes.io/region` and `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` on its node

### Optional

- `bgp` (Attributes) BGP peering of the instance. Needed when the Nest uses BGP. Changing it replaces the instance (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bgp))
- `etcd_disk` (Attributes) A disk of its own for etcd. Leave it out to keep etcd on the boot disk. Changing it replaces the instance (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--etcd_disk))

### Read-Only

- `architecture` (String) CPU architecture the instance reported once it booted
- `id` (Number) Internal ID of the Nest Instance on meltcloud
- `nest_id` (Number) ID of the Nest the instance belongs to
- `status` (String) Status of the instance: `installing` until it has joined the Nest, then `ready`. `boot_failed` if it reported a failed boot; see [Troubleshoot](https://docs.meltcloud.io/tasks/nest/troubleshoot#joining). A reset instance is `removed` until it installs again
- `version` (String) Nest version the instance runs

<a id="nestedatt--boot_disk"></a>
### Nested Schema for `boot_disk`

Required:

- `device` (String) Device the OS is installed to, for example `/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-1`. Use a `/dev/disk/by-path/` path rather than a kernel name such as `/dev/sda`, which can change between boots

Optional:

- `mirror` (Boolean) Mirror the boot disk onto a second device. Defaults to `false`
- `mirror_device` (String) Device the boot disk is mirrored to. Only with `mirror`


<a id="nestedatt--ip_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ip_addresses`

Required:

- `address` (String) The address the instance gets in that IP Pool
- `ip_pool_id` (Number) ID of the IP Pool the address is in


<a id="nestedatt--bgp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bgp`

Required:

- `local_asn` (Number) ASN of the instance
- `peers` (Attributes List) The BGP peers of the instance, each with its own address (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bgp--peers))

<a id="nestedatt--bgp--peers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bgp.peers`

Required:

- `asn` (Number) ASN of the peer
- `ip` (String) IP address of the peer

Optional:

- `bfd` (Attributes) Enables BFD on the session. Timings left out keep the defaults (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bgp--peers--bfd))
- `multihop` (Boolean) Enable if the peer is not directly connected (more than one hop away). Defaults to `false`
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive) Password of the BGP session. Write-only, needs Terraform 1.11 or later: it is not stored in the state. Changing `password_wo_version` replaces the instance. On an imported instance, set it to the password in use: the first version is recorded without a replace
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Version of `password_wo`, see there

<a id="nestedatt--bgp--peers--bfd"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bgp.peers.bfd`

Optional:

- `detect_multiplier` (Number) Detect multiplier
- `receive_interval` (Number) Receive interval in milliseconds
- `transmit_interval` (Number) Transmit interval in milliseconds




<a id="nestedatt--etcd_disk"></a>
### Nested Schema for `etcd_disk`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Keep etcd on a disk of its own

Optional:

- `device` (String) Device etcd is kept on. Only with `enabled`. Use a `/dev/disk/by-path/` path rather than a kernel name such as `/dev/sda`, which can change between boots
- `mirror` (Boolean) Mirror the etcd disk onto a second device. Defaults to `false`
- `mirror_device` (String) Device the etcd disk is mirrored to. Only with `mirror`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import meltcloud_nest_instance.nest_1 nest_instances/2
```
